# DSH-TokenDashboard
**Your local token usage, API calls, and cache activity in one dashboard.**
A lightweight plugin for DeepSeek Harness. No build step. No runtime dependencies. No additional API
htweight plugin for DeepSeek Harness. No build step. No runtime dependencies. No additional API key.
English · 简体中文
Features · Quick start · How counting works · FAQ
_Preview uses sample data. The plugin follows your DSH theme._
## Why DSH-TokenDashboard?
See how much you use across sessions, which projects drive token consumption, and how often your inp
ut hits the cache. The dashboard reads existing session logs in your current DSH profile and present
s the results inside the native sidebar.
## Features
| Feature                      | What you get
| Usage at a glance            | Total tokens, API calls, uncached input, output, cache reads, and c

ache hit rate              |
| Flexible summaries           | Last 7, 30, or 90 days, or all time, w

ith active session counts                               |
| Activity calendar            | 52 weeks

of square, rounded cells; hover or focus for exact daily numbers                     |
| Daily cache
trends           | Stacked input tokens: cache misses below cache hits, with a visible zero baselin

e             |
| Adjustable chart range       | Zoom from 7 to 30 days; compact K/M/B axis labels

|
| Model and project breakdowns | Token rankings and API

call counts by model/provider and working directory                    |
| Native presentation
| Light/dark themes, responsive layout, English and Simplified Chinese

|
| Refresh controls             | Manual refresh or automatic refresh every 30 seconds; polling pa
uses while the page is hidden |

On Windows, paths such as `C:/plugins/DSH-TokenDashboard` work as well. Quote paths that contain spa

### 3. Open the dashboard
Restart DSH and select **Usage statistics** in the sidebar. Existing completed requests appear autom
atically; the plugin does not need to run a new model request.

PIs. DSH plugin APIs may change between releases; check compatibility with your installed version.
## Using the dashboard

- Select a summary range at the top. Summary metrics and rankings follow this range.
- Hover over or
keyboard-focus a calendar cell or daily bar for exact usage and API call counts. Press **Escape** t

o dismiss the tooltip.
- Drag the trend slider to show the latest **7–30 days**. One month means a r

olling 30-day window.
- Calendar history and the trend window are independent of the summary range.

Changing that range preserves the trend zoom.
- Toggle automatic refresh at the bottom of the page.
## How counting works
| Metric         | Definition
| Total tokens   | Provider-reported `totalTokens`, or uncached input + output + cache reads + cache

writes when unavailable          |
| Input          | Uncached input only; excludes cache reads and

writes                                                               |
| Output         | Provider-
reported output; reasoning tokens are not added a second time

|
| Cache hit rate | Cache reads ÷ (uncached input + cache reads + cache writes); `—` when the

denominator is zero                      |
| API calls      | Settled `assistant/message` and `assi

stant/attempt` records, including settled failures and attempts without usage |
| Daily bars     | I
nput only: cache miss = uncached input + cache writes; cache hit = cache reads

|
| Sessions       | Sessions with at least one settled request in the selected summar
y range                                           |
An in-progress request appears after settlement. Requests without usage increase the API call count
but do not add estimated tokens. Repeated settlements for the same attempt are deduplicated; retry a
ttempts count separately, and inherited fork records are excluded.
[该节后续省略]
## Data and privacy
The plugin reads local session logs through read-only handles. It does not modify logs, call model A
PIs, or upload usage data. Numeric summaries, model names, session IDs, and working directories are
kept in memory for the dashboard; prompt and response content is not retained in that cache.
Each changed session is read in full before its numeric summary is cached by persistence revision. V
ery large logs can make the first load or a refresh slower. Unreadable sessions produce a visible pa
rtial-statistics warning.
This is a token accounting view, not a billing or network bandwidth meter. Provider billing may use
different accounting rules.
### Why is the dashboard empty?
It only sees the session data source available to the current DSH profile. Complete a request in tha
t profile, then refresh. Requests that are still streaming have not settled yet.
### Why do token totals differ from the provider's bill?
The dashboard uses usage reported in local logs and has no access to billing adjustments or external
requests. It does not estimate missing usage or calculate monetary costs.
### Why doesn't the chart match the selected summary period?
The activity calendar always covers 52 weeks. The daily chart has its own 7–30 day window and displa
ys input tokens only. The summary range applies to the headline metrics and rankings.
